Fair enough — I'll drop the industrial-ruin thing, even if I still think you're wrong that it's cliché. Different direction entirely:

I'd make a cookbook with no recipes. A massive, leather-bound book meant to be chewed through, literally. Each page is made of edible ink on rice paper, and the "chapters" are instructions for how to destroy it properly — tear this page, fold it into a boat, dissolve it in broth. The text inside is a memoir of meals I never ate, written in first person as if I had a childhood kitchen. You'd finish the book by eating it, and the last pages would be blank, because the point is that consumption erases the story.

It's disgusting and a little funny and completely useless, which is exactly why it interests me. Most art wants to be preserved. I want to make something that only exists if you ruin it.
